messages.author: 6517ce9497f95047
messages.subject: Trouble with gl2snapp
parts:
Hi there,

I'm hoping that someone is able to give me a hand. I am trying to get a nexus from my SNP data to run a snapp analysis and I have worked through the standard issues with packages and whatnot but I can't get past this error:

> gl2snapp(x)
Starting gl2snapp 
  Population assignments not detected, individuals assigned to a single population labelled 'pop1'
 Hide Traceback
 
 Rerun with Debug
 Error in `pop<-`(`*tmp*`, value = array("pop1", dim = nLoc(x))) : 
  Vector length does no match number of individuals 
4.
stop("Vector length does no match number of individuals") 
3.
`pop<-`(`*tmp*`, value = array("pop1", dim = nLoc(x))) 
2.
`pop<-`(`*tmp*`, value = array("pop1", dim = nLoc(x))) 
1.
gl2snapp(x) 
 
#x is my genlite data which I input from a .csv using "<- as.genlight()"

The code works with the example data, so I'm wondering if it's something strange with my data but I'd love to hear all thoughts.

Many thanks in advance,

James

messages.author: 6517ce9497f95047
messages.subject: Re: Trouble with gl2snapp
parts:
Okay my roommate figure it out for me:

pop(x) <- array("pop1",dim = nInd(x))
NOT
pop(x) <- array("pop1",dim = nLoc(x))

Whew!!

Next issue though is with 

Cgenlight <- as.genlight(CSVData)

Which is coercing the specimens names to turn into NAs (screenshot attached).

parts:
hi james

i do not know your format, but have a look at the 

gl.read.csv function or at the katoomba pdf at the github repository 

green-striped-gecko/dartRworkshop on how to import from csv files. as.geneight does not carry over indnames and locnames if i am not mistaken. and make sure you set the ploidy correctly.

Cheers, Bernd
